entities.name: Gebhard (III) of Constance
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Gebhard III, Bishop of Constance, played a pivotal role in defending papal rights against imperial encroachments during the Investiture Controversy (1056-1118). His efforts, which included the appointment of Conrad II as Emperor, contributed to the eventual resolution of the conflict through the Treaty of Worms (1122). Gebhard III's legacy as a champion of papal authority has endured, influencing the development of Catholic Church policies and the balance of power between the Church and secular institutions. The Investiture Controversy, in which Gebhard III was a key figure, reshaped the political landscape of Western Europe, setting the stage for the rise of the Holy Roman Empire. Gebhard III's actions also had a lasting impact on the development of canon law, which continues to shape Catholic doctrine and practice.
